body: “Boy, that escalated quickly!” While we don’t want to trivialize the Middle East war or the sell-off in markets since February, this memorable line uttered by Will Ferrell in *Anchorman* is one cheeky way to describe the about-face in market returns and risk appetite relative to January’s optimistic outlook. Despite the headwinds, we maintain our moderately overweight view on global equities over our 12-month horizon, for several reasons: The year began with strong earnings momentum, the AI innovation theme remains intact, valuations are more attractive, and fiscal policy remains supportive. We see some risk that markets are not pricing in the possibility of a more prolonged conflict and its economic spillover effects, but we also recognize that global markets entered the crisis with a healthy earnings buffer (quite different from the weakening in earnings leading into last year’s tariff shock) and that we could just as well see a de-escalation in the conflict.
